issue.title: Do no call `OkHttp#setRetryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for POST request
issue.body:
https://github.com/floating-cat/S1-Next/commit/382f95729eed00214b9da85b90d23e48cb93039a#diff-d2a554428ced185d821c8e3241eab312R37 call `OkHttp#setRetryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for POST request in order to avoid retries.

Looks this issue was caused by https://github.com/square/okhttp/issues/1146.
So current we do not disable retry for post request. If OkHttp still silently retries on POST request, than reopen this issue.

issue.title: Define policy on timeouts and retries

repository.name: okhttp
repository.description: Square’s meticulous HTTP client for the JVM, Android, and GraalVM.

issue.body:
@nfuller:

> Here: [HttpEngine.isRecoverable](https://github.com/square/okhttp/blob/master/okhttp/src/main/java/com/squareup/okhttp/internal/http/HttpEngine.java#L440)
> The catch should be treating SocketTimeoutException (which, you'll recall, is subclass of InterruptedIOException) as a "retryable". InterruptedIOException should probably still be non-retryable In this one case. The reasoning being that timeouts can be the result of misconfigured networking, but other InterruptedIOExceptions may be a call to Thread.interrupt() (e.g. issue #1146). Other cases still look like SocketTimeoutException should be treated the same as InterruptedIOException (to me) so shouldn't need to be changed, except to point out that the logic is no longer common.

I think we should figure out what we want the policy to be, and then implement that exactly. And I think we probably want the policy to be that timeouts are short (say _5_ or _10_ seconds by default) and retries are automatic.

We need to figure out how we count various things: do 3 SSL negotiations count as a single attempt? And how many attempts to we make to a webservice with 5 IP addresses?

Until now this hasn't really been decided, and it should be! Plus we should figure out what knobs to expose.

Related: https://github.com/square/okhttp/issues/1146
And of course this: https://twitter.com/mumak/status/628489427489288192

issue.title: Partially revert connection timeout behavior

repository.name: okhttp
repository.description: Square’s meticulous HTTP client for the JVM, Android, and GraalVM.

issue.body:
Related to issue #1790.

If there is a _connection_ timeout the next route should
be tried. Timeouts during a request/response should
probably not be retried.

The timeout/interrupt behavior was changed in PR #1257
for issue #1146. This modified both connection and
request/response behavior. The issue reported was actually
about the use of Thread.interrupt(), not timeouts, but the
behavior change modified both behavior for interrupt and
timeout.

PR #1388 split the handling of exceptions so that separate
code now handles connection errors from that which handles
request/response errors. It faithfully kept the behavior
from PR #1257.

The modification of the timeout behavior during _connection_
caused problems on Android. Now that the two types of error
handling are split it's possible to deal with them
differently and return the connection behavior to trying
the next route. This does not modify behavior during
request/response.

A test has been added for timeouts. It does not seem to be
possible to interrupt a Socket.connect() call with
Thread.interrupt() on either OpenJDK or Android so a
placeholder has been implemented. If it ever is implemented
a Thread.interrupt() during connect will not be retried.
